subject: Critical: PayFlux checkout 5xx spike — executive bridge request
messages:
From: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@payflux.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 22:30:00 -0800
Subject: Checkout 5xx / latency surge — we need immediate help

Karthik —

We started seeing an abrupt spike in 5xx errors at ~22:00 PST. The checkout flow is timing out for ~37% of requests and overall p95 latency is up to 3.1s (normally ~350ms). We rolled back our last edge config and there was a brief improvement but it returned.

Sample error from our logs attached (payflux-error-20261109.log). Metrics are attached as CSV. This is affecting our peak window; we are already seeing failed charges and customer complaints.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is an inference degradation on the model variant we pinned (gpt-neo-quant-v2)? We're seeing a lot of 502/504 from the Redwood proxy in our traces. If we need to failover to a compatible lighter variant, we need guidance and a rollback window.

We'd like an executive bridge — PayFlux leadership is asking for immediate coordination.

— Liam
Director of Platform Engineering
PayFlux

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@payflux.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 07:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Checkout 5xx / latency surge — we need immediate help

Liam — thanks for the heads-up and for the artifacts. We see the same error signature in our edge telemetry (large tail in queue wait + sporadic 502s from the model instances).

Immediate plan (10:00 PST war-room):
- 07:30 PST: internal tech triage (runtime + infra) — David and Marissa to lead.
- 08:30 PST: customer sync / runbook review (Laura to lead customer comms).
- 10:00 PST: Executive bridge (Markus and I will join) — coordinate with PayFlux leadership.

Requests for your team before 08:30 PST:
1) Grab a 5–10 minute HAR or trace from a failed checkout and drop in the thread.
2) Note the exact model variant you pinned and any recent pin/rollout changes.
3) Confirm whether you have an internal fallback to a cached result path (we can coordinate a short-lived traffic split).

Attachments: please see the log and metrics you attached — we'll pull additional telemetry on our side.

I am marking this as high priority and invoking the throughput/latency playbook. If we need to enact an automatic fallback to a smaller model, we'll propose a canary traffic-shift and a short SLA credit as a mitigation.

-Karthik
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:15:40 -0800
Subject: Re: Checkout 5xx / latency surge — we need immediate help

Karthik / team —

Triage status at 08:15 PST:
- Infra: a subset of model instances on us-west-2 are exhibiting elevated kernel stalls when sequence lengths exceed 1024 (we're correlating with a sudden uptick in long queries from PayFlux).
- Serving runtime: queue depth is rising due to a mismatch in batching cadence under the current autoscale window.

Immediate actions (assigned):
- David: pull instance-level kernel logs and isolate unhealthy workers (we'll OOS them).
- Me (Marissa): coordinate a temporary reduction in max sequence length via request-side enforcement (client-side guard) and suggest a 20% traffic split to the quant-light variant.
- Laura: prepare external comm and runbook for PayFlux execs.

I'm attaching a CSV of the per-instance error rates (payflux-metrics-20261109.csv). I recommend we start a controlled canary to the lighter variant at 09:00 PST, observe 30min, then widen if stable.

—Marissa
Head of Incident Ops
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:52:05 -0800
Subject: Re: Checkout 5xx / latency surge — customer comm draft

Liam / PayFlux leadership —

Thanks for the patience while we triage. Below is a short draft we can use for customer-facing comms; please review and tell us if you want different framing. We intend to send this once we have a stable mitigation in place (controlled canary to the lighter variant).

DRAFT: 
Subject: Service disruption affecting checkout processing — temporary mitigation in progress
Body:
Hi team,

We're investigating an elevated error rate impacting checkout operations. Our vendor (Redwood Inference) has identified a subset of model instances experiencing processing delays when handling unusually long prompt sequences. Redwood is executing a mitigation plan that includes routing a portion of traffic to a lighter model variant, stabilizing latency and reducing failed requests. We will provide another update within one hour and a post-incident summary once resolved.

If you have immediate concerns, contact PayFlux platform (platform@payflux.com) or our on-call.

---

Proposed external ask to PayFlux: authorize a 20% canary to the quant-light variant at 09:00 PST. Approve or suggest modifications.

Operational notes for exec bridge:
- Expected impact window: 09:00–10:30 PST while we measure canary performance.
- If canary shows >1.5x baseline error or p95 remains >1s, we'll widen fallback and consider manual routing to dedicated capacity.

Link to draft doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBzPayFlux-comm-draft

—Laura
Director, Customer Success Ops
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@payflux.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 03:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Checkout 5xx / latency surge — executive bridge request

Team / PayFlux execs —

Thanks — quick update ahead of today's bridge at 10:00 PST:
- 09:00 PST: initiated 20% canary to quant-light variant. Early telemetry at +18 minutes: error rate back down to ~4% on the canary path, p95 on canary ~420ms.
- 09:45 PST: will have a 30-minute rolling check to decide widening to 50%.
- If we widen, we will monitor customer-facing telemetry and prepare an SLA credit estimate for PayFlux for the degraded window.

Immediate asks for exec bridge:
1) Markus — be prepared to authorize a comm signoff and the estimated credit envelope.
2) David / Marissa — bring runbook metrics and escalations ladder.
3) Laura — bring the customer comm with signoffs and a proposed send time (we prefer a single coordinated message once the 50% decision is made).

Liam — please standby for the 10:00 PST executive call. We'll share a short readout deck and the incident timeline.

-Karthik
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
